project.title: Central Wire Industries Infrastructure Manager

role_overview.summary: Central Wire Industries is a $500 million annual revenue wire manufacturing enterprise operating across multiple physical sites in the United States and Canada. Christian served as Operations and Infrastructure Manager, responsible for all aspects of IT infrastructure across the organization's expanded footprint. The engagement spanned an M&A IT integration following the acquisition of TechAlloy Inc. from ArcelorMittal, enterprise backup standardization, unified communications consolidation, smart-factory integration, and enterprise-wide payroll system consolidation — the latter two following a 60% growth period driven by site acquisitions. Christian delivered all initiatives under waterfall methodology, managing vendor relationships, regulatory compliance requirements spanning US DOD NOFORN, ISO:27001, and NIST, and multi-stakeholder requirements gathering across production, HR, finance, and executive teams. Infrastructure management operations ran continuously from May 2007 across all nine sites in the United States and Canada.

challenge.summary: Central Wire Industries underwent significant growth through acquisition, expanding from 5 to 9 sites across the United States and Canada. Each acquisition introduced fragmented IT environments — incompatible ERP platforms, disconnected telephony systems, unmanaged backup practices, and disparate network infrastructure — requiring a structured programme of IT integration, standardization, and compliance alignment across the full enterprise footprint.

solution.summary: Delivered comprehensive infrastructure management and project delivery across:
deliverables: M&A IT Integration — TechAlloy Inc. Acquisition (ERP consolidation, AD migration, WAN buildout)
Enterprise Backup Standardization & WAN File Services (LTO-5 / Veritas Backup Exec / Microsoft DFS — 8 sites)
Enterprise Telephony Consolidation — Avaya Unified Communications (9-site rollout)
IT Integration of fully automated production systems (Fond du Lac, Wisconsin — GE Fanuc / SCADA / AS/400)
ADP Payroll Systems Migration (Citrix Virtualization, Platform Upgrade, Database Migration — 9 sites)

outcomes: Completed M&A IT integration of TechAlloy Inc. (acquired from ArcelorMittal) within 13 months, onboarding three US manufacturing sites and approximately 100 users onto the consolidated Central Wire Active Directory domain

Retired two legacy Syteline ERP instances across five factories, consolidating all manufacturing operations onto the superior AS/400-based Lawson MOVEX and INFOR BPCS platform, delivering approximately $8,000/year in software savings and approximately $12,000 per hardware refresh cycle

Standardized enterprise data protection across all eight sites with LTO-5 tape libraries and Veritas Backup Exec, establishing offsite vaulting via Vital Records Inc. (VRI) under a 10-year retention policy — eliminating ad-hoc backup practices including at least one site with no viable backup media

Unified enterprise telephony across nine previously disconnected sites via Avaya, enabling inter-site call routing, Follow-Me mobility, and intelligent outbound call routing that eliminated avoidable long-distance and international call charges

Integrated GE Fanuc smart-factory automation and SCADA systems into centralized AS/400-based Lawson MOVEX and INFOR BPCS ERP/MRP suites, delivering lights-out manufacturing capability at the Fond du Lac facility
Implemented IT security controls meeting US DOD NOFORN classification with ISO:27001 and NIST compliance

Consolidated ADP payroll services across 9 physical sites in the United States and Canada following 60% growth, delivering cross-border HR and Finance access via Citrix virtualization with RBAC access controls meeting ISO:27001 and NIST compliance
